depth: The depth map presents an elevated view of a construction site as the camera wearer pans left over five frames. Frame 1 looks toward a wall about 1–1.5 m away, with a vertical wooden pole (~0.5 m, within the wearer’s arm’s reach) and a white pipe (~1 m) before it. Frames 2–5 expose an open ground space below and on the left, where sacks, buckets, and pans sit at approximately 1.5–4 m. Two workers occupy the lower ground roughly 0.8–1 m apart: the closer pink-shirted person (~2–2.5 m from the wearer, facing right toward the wall and away from the camera) is partly hidden by the foreground wooden pole and suspended ropes (~0.5–0.8 m, within the wearer’s arm’s reach), while the more distant plaid-shirted person stands behind and left (~3–3.5 m away), shifting from a right-facing orientation in Frame 2 to facing and looking toward the wearer in Frames 3–5. The ground-level bucket, pans, and wooden pole are within the two workers’ arm’s reach, and the foreground pole and hanging ropes stay within the camera wearer’s reach in every frame. The map makes the uninterrupted distance gradient along the right-side wall and ground plane clearer, as well as the foreground separation between the pole and hanging ropes and the workers below, which is more difficult to estimate in the cluttered RGB view. Nevertheless, depth is unreliable within the rope loops, where background-wall pixels bleed through at bright foreground depth, and across the upper-left background in Frames 2–5, where rubble and walls merge into uniformly black saturation.
segmentation: After finding no objects in Frame 1, the segmentation map separates distinct foreground entities in Frames 2–5. It identifies the two standing workers (~2–2.5 m and ~3–3.5 m from the camera wearer and ~0.8–1 m apart), plus one metal pan classified as a “bowl” on the ground to their left (~3.5 m away) in Frames 3–5. From the wearer’s viewpoint, the plaid-shirted worker stands behind and slightly left of the pink-shirted worker. The detected bowl lies below and left of both workers’ feet, just outside their immediate arm’s reach, although nearer buckets and sacks that are within reach remain unlabeled. As the camera pans left and then steadies during Frames 2–5, the masks depict the pink-shirted worker bending forward toward the right-hand wall in Frame 5, while the plaid-shirted worker remains upright and rotates his torso and head toward the camera wearer. In Frames 3–5, the map supplies crisp silhouette edges that distinguish the neighboring workers from the similarly colored dirt, sacks, and plastered wall. It is unreliable in Frame 2, however, because the foreground wooden pole and ropes divide the pink-shirted worker into several overlapping “person” masks that incorrectly absorb parts of the pole and rope. It also exchanges the workers’ instance colours in Frame 5 and does not segment the pipes, poles, sacks, buckets, or remaining pans.
pose: Only one worker in each frame receives a yellow 2D body skeleton from Frame 2 through Frame 5; the pose map leaves out the camera wearer and every object in the scene. In Frame 2, it follows the farther plaid-shirted worker (~3–3.5 m away on the left), who faces right and extends his right arm downward toward the pink-shirted worker positioned ~0.8–1 m ahead of him. Despite substantial clutter in the RGB imagery, the skeleton clearly conveys the worker’s profile direction, shoulder-to-hip alignment, increasing forward bend in Frame 5, and the placement of his legs behind the obstructing foreground pole.
